LLM_Annotation.sentence: I have been a patient of Dr. Norman Lavin's for about 10 years now. He literally saved my life!!! I have a very rare disease that was causing my health and function to seriously deteriorate over a span of about 2 years, and NO other doctors were able to figure out why--for almost 2 years, I had numerous hospital stays and even a long, horrible nursing home stay before I was referred to Dr. Lavin. He never gave up on me! He knew which scans, labs, etc. to order for me, and now I am finally being treated for the disease almost 10 years and have as much of my life back as I can. (There is no cure for the disease, but at least the treatment is helping me live my life.) I am sad to see all the negative reviews here on Yelp. I have NOT had most the experiences described here--I usually have wait times of maybe up to 10 minutes, just like I do at most my other doctors' offices. If I had to choose between shorter wait times or shorter visits with the doctor, well, I think it's more important that Dr. Lavin spends the time with each patient that they need, so I don't mind waiting. And just like with other doctors, I have found that if you can educate yourself the best you can about your condition and be super proactive while you are with the doctor (write down all questions you have for the doctor and bring to your appointment, speak up, find out what your most recent labs/scans show and ask him to explain it to you, etc.), you will have a more positive experience with him. I remember only one occasion I had an appointment with Dr. Lavin when I had looked down briefly and when I looked back up, he was gone--so I went to the front desk and asked them to chase him down for me because I wasn't done with him yet, LOL--and they did, and by the time I left, I felt confident that I had gotten everything I needed from the doctor that day. Dr. Lavin really does have a heart of gold. He really does care about his patients. The nutritionist Kristine has a heart of gold, too, and she is super smart! She will spend as much time as needed getting answers for you, even after she has left for the day--she is also awesome in that she doesn't give up on you. As far as the front desk is concerned, Randi is the person to talk to (I think she's the office manager) if you have any questions, concerns, issues, etc., though you might need to wait till she's off the phone--she and the rest of the staff spend a LOT of time on the phone because they are speaking to your insurance company, your pharmacy, etc. which can be a huge time suck, but that part is not their fault. Randi has worked for Dr. Lavin a long time--she was there when I first became a patient 10 years ago, and she is very knowledgeable and she also has a heart of gold and cares about the patients. My first 5-7 years coming to Dr. Lavin's, the other front desk staff were the same, too--very helpful, kind, efficient, you know their names and they know you when they see you, but I have also noticed that only in the past few years, most of them are gone and now there are new faces, I don't know all of them, they don't know me, and it can be frustrating every once in a while. I, too, have found that sometimes it is hard to get ahold of them on the phone, but that is also true of some of my other doctors' offices. But in the end, it is all offset by getting to see a doctor who is so smart he probably graduated top of his class, who is smarter than pretty much any other doctor around here, and who is smart enough to figure out how to help me when no one else could.
label: Referred to Dr. Lavin after having numerous hospital stays and issues with other doctors

LLM_Annotation.sentence:
Looking for an ENT? Just don't.
I've been dealing with sinus issues for many years and a family member suggested a balloon rhinoplasty to open my passages. The doctor was nice, however I felt like the procedure was somewhat pushed on me upon my first visit -- no alternatives except for gutting out my sinuses, which is a more evasive procedure. I agreed and it was scheduled. I was told that the outpatient procedure would take me out of work for an avg of 2 1/2 days. Although I haven't had any issues post-op, I wish I wouldn't have been awake for what I witnessed after I was numbed up. 
If you're non-religious, then you should know that he'll ask to say a prayer prior to the procedure. He then pulled in 3 other people into that small room to observe (although one 'observer' assisted), and let's just say that it wasn't a walk in the park. He grinds a tube between your canine teeth and your gums to allow the balloon to enter your sinuses, but they don't tell you about the CRUNCH that occurs once the balloon is inflated. Personally, I don't like people messing around in my skull when I'm awake except for my dentist! 
The billing fiasco is another story all together. During the procedure the doctor said that there's no charge for the followup. Upon scheduling, the person on the line said that there is no followup to the procedure (yet they do this to charge your insurance as a regular visit.) Remember when I wrote that the doctor said 'no charge'? They charge your insurance either way and you have to pickup the remainder. So it's really a deferred charge. They said that it's a courtesy that they don't have you pay a copay upon arrival and that they bill your insurance first to see if they'll cover it. The doctor shouldn't say something as stupid as 'no charge' when he doesn't know how his billing works. The bill was only $25, but it's the principle of the matter, you know.
I won't be stepping foot back into this office. I don't care if they gave me a free t-shirt -- I'm burning it!
label: Family member suggested a procedure

LLM_Annotation.sentence: I injured both knees two years ago, training for a marathon.  I always dreamed of running an ironman triathlon but suffered from chronic injury.  I made another attempt recently yet I could not handle even small amounts of running.  Both knees did not recover.  I found myself unable to run even for 5 minutes.  It felt hopeless and I was convinced that I was just not going to be able to run at all.  Despite stopping running, the pain did not get better.  I was worried that I would need surgery.  I am a physician and despite my medical training and experience with running, became extremely frustrated with myself, the injuries, and lack of good guidance.  I looked for an orthopedic surgeon who had experience with athletes.  I did not just want to be able to walk pain-free.  I wanted to run and ride my bike as often as I wanted.  I found Dr. Stetson's office.  When I walked into the office, I noticed all the large autographed pictures of olympic athletes on the walls.  I had come to the right place.  Dr. Stetson took my athletic endeavors seriously and I was happy that he did not write me off and say to give up on running.  An MRI showed a small injury to the medial meniscus and some arthritis under the patella.  Dr. Stetson said we should see if we can improve this with conservative measures and physical therapy.  I was appreciative of this conservative approach and felt better that we had a plan.  The subsequent few months were difficult.  I felt that I was making zero improvement.  I found out I had some major muscle weaknesses that were contributing to my pain.  I was neither running nor cycling, just doing therapy.  I kept doing the exercises.  By the beginning of the new year I started to notice some improvement.  I continued physical therapy on my own and learned to run again.  This is a hard part of recovery and requires persistence and retraining the way the brain and the muscles communicate.  I started running 5 minutes at a time.  10 minutes at a time the next week, and so on.  Dr. Stetson saw me from time to time and encouraged me to be patient.  I began to alternate swimming, cycling, and running.  I slowly progressed.  I still had pain from time to time but I felt that I wanted to give triathlon another try.  By this point I had built a small group of experts who got to know me and supported me: Dr. Stetson's team, the physical therapists at Core Conditioning, Lisa the massage and ART specialist at LA bodywork, and my training coach.  I began to struggle again with pain.  Dr. Stetson was confident we could get the pain under control.  His bedside manner is exemplary and he always remembered me.  He made good decisions.  I turned a corner last winter and was able to achieve up to 4 hour bike rides.  Soon thereafter was able to run for 2.5 hours at a time.  I was not certain if I was going to complete the ironman distance but I was happy, just happy being active.  As I got to within 1 month of the race, I developed some swelling behind my left knee and some snapping in the hamstring tendon.  Stephanie the PA saw me with no notice and was able to rule out any serious problem which reassured me that I was going to be ok.  In July, I completed my first ever Ironman triathlon: 2.4 mile swim, 112 mile bike ride, and a 26.2 mile run.  I had a fantastic race and finished the event with no problem.  Not only did I finish but I was able to run the entire marathon.  It was an unbelievable journey of pain and frustration where I went from not being able to run nor bike and then in 2 years finish an ironman with no pain.  I cannot tell you how good it felt to cross that finish line.  I returned a week after my race to Dr. Stetson's clinic to get an MRI of the knee and it was normal.  I learned so much from this experience.  Most importantly I learned that it takes an incredible amount of patience, knowledge, and support from many different people to help you through an injury.  While it may not be possible for everyone to run an ironman, people can and often do more than they believe they can.  People deserve to be able to move their bodies without pain and to have good doctors that they trust absolutely.  Dr. Stetson was in my corner from day 1.  I walked into his office and was prepared for him to tell me I needed surgery.  And I trust Dr. Stetson to operate on me.  In the beginning I was feeling very impatient.  I wanted a magic bullet to just make things normal.  Unfortunately life and the human body does not work so easily.  I have come to appreciate that what truly makes a surgeon great is not just performing successful operations, but also having the knowledge and experience to know when to not operate.  I appreciate that Dr. Stetson had the patience to guide me even when I did not.  A big heartfelt thank you to Dr. Stetson, Stephanie, the medical students, and the entire staff at Stetson Powell Orthopedics sports medicine clinic.  Thank you for helping me make a dream come true.
label: Referred by personal search for an orthopedic surgeon

I found out via a regular routine ultrasound in the office at 12 weeks that there was no heartbeat and after that my OB very quickly wrapped up the appointment and told me I needed a d&c. She recommneded that I go to a private practice to have it done but left the room without providing any information about the practice (location, phone number) and I had to go into the main nurse area to be like "um hello can someone let me know where I'm supposed to go for this?" The d&c was totally fine and I had them send a chromosomal sample for testing to find out if there was a cause for it, and the d&c doc said they'd send the results back to my OB. After 3 months of waiting I hadn't received a call from my OB to follow up to see how I was doing post miscarriage, which maybe was unrealistic to expect? Nor had I received any follow up info related to my d&c results. Finally I called labcorp and got the results directly through them but also confirmed they'd send them to my OB, which they had. After a few calls to my OB office a nurse finally called me back and said they had my results and my OB would call me within the next few days to review the results. It has been 2 months and she has yet to call me back. I ended up forwarding my d&c results to my fertility specialist who is wonderful and got back to me about them within 24 hours. So after this I decided to leave the practice for a more compassionate and responsive provider. Hopefully my experience is not the norm here and somehow something slipped through the cracks but it was incredibly disappointing and pretty awful patient care. Maybe they have no idea how to handle anything other than simple routine OB and pregnancy care but given the % of women who miscarry I would expect a big practice like this to have MUCH better in office and follow up care regarding miscarriages. It made the whole experience even worse than it already was.
label: Referred by OB recommendation to a private practice for d&c

Last year an acute kidney stone pain episode brought me to this office.   Initially I got my appointment very quickly.  Doctor Saltzman convinced me for a more invasive procedure and able to book me into the hospital in two days.  The day of the procedure was the beginning of my nightmare.  I remembered after wakeup from the procedure at the recovery room, the doctor has long gone.  yes, doctor took off for a long weekend and I never saw doctors after the procedure at the hospital.  The nurse at the hospital told me that doctor did not perform the procedure he recommended, instead he put a stent into the tube and my stone was still inside.  But the unexpected stent caused more bleeding and pain over the weekend which required much stronger dose of pain control medication.   I called on call doctor for the office, it turns out Dr. Saltzman's brother is on call doctor at the time.  He picked up the first call from me and told me bleeding and pain were expected, then I was never able to reach him again.   My weekend pain was much worse than before the procedure and was knocked off by morphine till very next Monday when I finally able to talk with the office and requested to remove the stent ASAP.  A few days later, I granted an appointment and office told me removing stent procedure will be in their own office and they do this "all the time".  But I did not realize that this office has no nurse on payroll.  That's right, no nurse in this office, yet they perform medical procedure all the time.  During my procedure, the office manager/admin girl was called in to the room as assistance.  When I ask her question, she said that " I don't know, I am not nurse, I am only an office admin personnel".  She confirmed that there is no nurse in this office.  
After this experience, I fortunately got another appointment with an reputable urologist from B&W hospital, B&W doctor confirmed that Dr. Saltzman initially recommended invasive procedure would not be his preferred option based on my image data.  
This office is in a mission for more profit.  They shuffle people in and out very quick.  My advice is do yourself a favor, stay away from this office.

LLM_Annotation.sentence: One day I noticed a birthmark on my leg which looked more like a dysplastic (irregular shape and colors) than regular mole. I knew that with this kind of birthmarks we must be very careful and we should run to doctor ASAP. So I went to NFDERM to look for a help. Dr Jonathan Kantor obviously didn't have any idea about possible melanoma procedures and he cut my mole just from the surface to send it to laboratory. Later I've found out from different dr that should never be done! Every mole looking like mine should be cut with the healthy skin margin to prevent bad cells spreading through the blood cells. Jonathan Kantor didn't know that!! and 2 weeks later he called me for another cut because the mole happened to be dysplastic. he made the surgery on my skin and left me with 12 stitches scar and sent my skin to laboratory again. I didn't have insurance and all that was very costly for me (around 1000$). Beside that I never was paid too big attention to. I asked him many questions but got no answers, felt very ignored. I was very scared but dr never tried to calm me down. After all that bad experience I've found another dermatologist. Much more professional, when I've got another irreguar mole he cut it with the margin and left me with 5 stitches. I paid around 300$ without the necessity of another surgery. I wish I could be warned before I made my choice about the doctor. Now I'm warning all of you who read that. Jonathan Kantor is realy not worth to be your specialist!
